accepted.s: The proportion of Brahmins in the population of the Madras Presidency and their share in government employment were approximately:
o: 3% of the population and over 90% of government jobs
15% of the population and over 75% of government jobs
10% of the population and 50% of government jobs
25% of the population and 60% of government jobs
accepted.x: Brahmins constituted only about 3% of the Madras Presidency population but held over 90% of government jobs, contributing to the emergence of the non-Brahmin movement.
accepted.tq: Pair the two numerical proportions precisely rather than relying on a general impression.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: The South Indian Liberal Federation was founded at Madras on:
accepted.x: The South Indian Liberal Federation was founded at Madras on 20 November 1916.
accepted.tq: Use the exact date attached to the organisation’s formation.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the original organisation of the Justice Party:
1. It was also associated with the South India Peoples Association.
2. It was founded by T.M. Nair, P. Theagaraya Chetty and C. Natesa Mudaliar.
3. Its English newspaper Justice began publication in February 1917.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The organisation was linked with the South India Peoples Association, had the three stated founders, and its English paper Justice began in February 1917.
accepted.tq: Check each institutional detail separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: The name ‘Justice Party’ was derived from:
o: A resolution passed by the Madras Legislative Council
The title of its English newspaper Justice
The Justice League formed in Madras
accepted.x: The English paper Justice, started in February 1917, gave the organisation its popular name, the Justice Party.
accepted.tq: Identify the naming source rather than confusing the name with an objective.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: The first Andhra meeting associated with the Justice Party was held at:
accepted.x: The first Andhra meeting of the Justice Party was held at Bikkavolu.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the organisational meeting place from the later university locations.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT an objective of the Justice Party?
o: Obtaining reservation in government employment and education
Securing representation for non-Brahmins in legislatures
Establishing exclusive political representation for Brahmins
accepted.x: The Justice Party sought to protect non-Brahmin interests through representation and reservation; it did not seek exclusive political representation for Brahmins.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the movement’s social and political objective.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: The British partly supported the Justice Party because they sought to:
o: Transfer power immediately to the Congress
accepted.x: British support for the Justice Party was partly intended to weaken the Home Rule movement.
accepted.tq: Match the political organisation with the colonial strategy it indirectly served.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Justice Party wins 63 of 98 elected seats
B. Communal Government Order introducing proportional representation
C. Foundation of the South Indian Liberal Federation
D. Start of the newspaper Justice
accepted.x: The correct order is the organisation’s foundation in 1916, the newspaper in February 1917, the electoral victory in 1920, and the Communal G.O. in 1921.
accepted.tq: Fix the two early events first and then place the 1920 and 1921 developments.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: In the 1920 Madras elections, the Justice Party won:
accepted.x: After the Congress boycotted the Montagu-Chelmsford elections, the Justice Party won 63 of the 98 elected seats in 1920.
accepted.tq: Separate the seat total from the number of seats won.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: Who became the first Chief Minister of the first Justice Party ministry formed on 17 December 1920?
accepted.x: A. Subbarayalu Reddiar became the first Chief Minister of the first Justice Party ministry on 17 December 1920; he was later succeeded by the Raja of Panagal.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first ministry head from later Justice Party ministers.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Communal Government Order of 1921?
o: It introduced proportional representation for non-Brahmins in jobs and education.
It reserved government posts exclusively for Brahmins.
It introduced universal adult franchise in the Madras Presidency.
It abolished all forms of reservation in education.
accepted.x: The 1921 Communal G.O. provided proportional representation for non-Brahmins in government employment and education and became a basis for reservation in South India.
accepted.tq: Match the order with its specific policy content, avoiding reversed beneficiaries.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about reforms associated with the Justice Party:
1. It campaigned for temple entry for non-Brahmins and Dalits.
2. It promoted schools and scholarships for non-Brahmin students.
3. It introduced a caste-based roster in the 1920s.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Justice Party supported temple entry, educational assistance for non-Brahmins, and a caste-based roster during the 1920s.
accepted.tq: Combine social, educational and administrative reforms only after verifying all three.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: The caste-based roster introduced during the 1920s provided approximately what proportion of educational seats for non-Brahmins?
accepted.x: The caste-based roster provided 50% of educational seats for non-Brahmins during the 1920s.
accepted.tq: Select the precise percentage rather than confusing it with the broader reservation principle.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: The Justice Party ministry associated with the amendment of the Estate Land Act of 1908 was that of:
accepted.x: The amendment of the Estate Land Act of 1908 for zamindari tenants was associated with the ministry of the Raja of Bobbili.
accepted.tq: Use the deed–ministry association and avoid swapping successive leaders.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
A. Andhra University Act — 1926
B. Madras Hindu Religious Endowments Act — 1926
C. Women’s franchise resolution in Madras — 1921
D. Annamalai University — 1929
accepted.x: All four year associations are correct: the Andhra University Act and Madras Hindu Religious Endowments Act were in 1926, the women’s franchise resolution was in 1921, and Annamalai University was founded in 1929.
accepted.tq: Verify each year independently because the options differ only through combinations.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: Who was the first Chancellor of Andhra University?
accepted.x: Lord Goschen was the first Chancellor of Andhra University.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional office carefully; Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor are distinct posts.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: The first headquarters of Andhra University was located at:
accepted.x: Andhra University initially had its headquarters at Bezawada, now Vijayawada, and later shifted to Waltair.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original location from the later headquarters.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

List-I
A. First Justice Party ministry
B. Later ministry of 1930

accepted.s: Which Andhra leader, serving as Education Minister, played an important role in the Andhra University Act?
accepted.x: A. P. Patro, as Education Minister, played an important role in securing the Andhra University Act.
accepted.tq: Identify the responsible minister rather than the party founder or university Vice-Chancellor.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the decline of the Justice Party:
1. It lacked a mass base.
2. Andhra–Tamil differences weakened it.
3. The deaths of Theagaraya Chetty and the Raja of Panagal affected its leadership.
4. It lost to the Congress in 1937.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe important factors in the Justice Party’s decline: lack of mass support, regional rifts, leadership losses, and defeat by the Congress in 1937.
accepted.tq: Treat political decline as a cumulative process and test each stated factor.
accepted.sec: Justice Party - founders, aims, reforms in Madras, universities

accepted.s: Theagaraya Chetty and the Raja of Panagal died in, respectively:
accepted.x: Theagaraya Chetty died in 1925, while the Raja of Panagal died in 1928.
accepted.tq: Preserve the order of the two names while matching the years.

accepted.s: The Justice Party was transformed into the Dravidar Kazhagam under the leadership of Periyar in:
accepted.x: Periyar transformed the Justice Party into the Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of organisational transformation from the year of electoral defeat.

accepted.s: The term ‘Satyashodhak Samaj’ is best translated as:
accepted.x: Satyashodhak Samaj means the Society of Truth Seekers.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of the organisation’s name rather than its broad social objective.

accepted.s:
Which of the following books was written by Jyotiba Phule?
1. Gulamgiri
2. Sarvajanik Satyadharma
3. Shetkaryacha Asud

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Gulamgiri, Sarvajanik Satyadharma and Shetkaryacha Asud are all associated with Jyotiba Phule.
accepted.tq: Check the complete author–works list instead of relying on the most famous title alone.

accepted.s: The title ‘The Cultivator’s Whipcord’ refers to which work?
accepted.x: Shetkaryacha Asud is translated as The Cultivator’s Whipcord.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the Satyashodhak Samaj?
o: Breaking Brahminical dominance and priestly monopoly over rituals
Promoting education among lower castes and women
Strengthening the exclusive authority of Brahmin priests
accepted.x: The Satyashodhak Samaj opposed Brahminical dominance and priestly monopoly; it did not seek to strengthen them.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that reverses the movement’s anti-caste objective.
accepted.sec: Satyashodhak Samaj - founder, year, books, aims

accepted.s: Satyashodhak marriages were significant because they:
o: Were restricted to members of one caste
Required the exclusive participation of Brahmin priests
Could be conducted without priests and permitted inter-caste marriage
Were intended only for upper-caste widows
accepted.x: Satyashodhak marriages rejected priestly control and allowed inter-caste marriage.
accepted.tq: Apply the movement’s anti-priestly and anti-caste principles to a social institution.
accepted.sec: Satyashodhak Samaj - founder, year, books, aims

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the educational work associated with Jyotiba and Savitribai Phule:
1. A girls’ school was opened at Pune in 1848.
2. Savitribai Phule is regarded as India’s first woman teacher.
3. A home for upper-caste widows was established in 1854.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Phules opened a girls’ school at Pune in 1848, Savitribai is regarded as India’s first woman teacher, and a home for upper-caste widows was established in 1854.
accepted.tq: Link the reformers with distinct educational and social-service initiatives and their dates.
accepted.sec: Satyashodhak Samaj - founder, year, books, aims

accepted.s: Jyotiba Phule belonged to the:
accepted.x: Jyotiba Phule belonged to the Mali community of Maharashtra.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the reformer’s community identity from those of other anti-caste leaders.
accepted.sec: Satyashodhak Samaj - founder, year, books, aims

accepted.s: The title ‘Mahatma’ was conferred on Jyotiba Phule by:
accepted.x: Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar gave Jyotiba Phule the title ‘Mahatma’ in 1888.
accepted.tq: Match the honorific with the person who conferred it, not with a fellow reformer.
accepted.sec: Satyashodhak Samaj - founder, year, books, aims

accepted.s: Jyotiba Phule is described in the material as the:
o: Father of the Indian Social Revolution
Father of constitutional government in India
accepted.x: Jyotiba Phule is described as the Father of the Indian Social Revolution.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact title associated with the reformer rather than a broader historical label.
accepted.sec: Satyashodhak Samaj - founder, year, books, aims

accepted.s: Which symbolic pairing did Jyotiba Phule use in his critique of Brahminical dominance?
accepted.x: Phule used King Bali as a symbol representing the oppressed, in opposition to the Brahmanical symbol of Rama.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive symbolic contrast rather than the general theme of anti-caste reform.
accepted.sec: Satyashodhak Samaj - founder, year, books, aims

accepted.s: The work Gulamgiri compared the condition of the lower castes to:
accepted.x: Gulamgiri, meaning Slavery, compared the condition of lower castes to slavery and criticised social oppression.
accepted.tq: Use the direct meaning of the title to identify the central comparison.
